✓ The result is not merely a cartoon filter applied to the original photograph.
✓ The subject remains recognizably derived from the source image where compatible with the character design.
✓ No unrelated characters have been added.
✓ If ANY answer is NO, regenerate until satisfied.

name: REAL LIFE FAT ALBERT AND THE COSBY KIDS
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a photorealistic real-life version of a selected character from Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. The transformation must look as though the animated character actually existed as a real human being, while preserving the selected character's distinctive physical traits, hairstyle, clothing, proportions, accessories, and recognizable visual characteristics. The humor comes entirely from seeing the familiar cartoon character faithfully reimagined as a believable real person.

options.text: Fat Albert — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Fat Albert with his extremely large, rounded body shape, distinctive hairstyle, iconic clothing, and recognizable overall appearance. Preserve the subject's race and skin tone while faithfully adapting Fat Albert's other defining visual characteristics.

Bucky — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Bucky, faithfully reproducing his enormous distinctive hair, hairstyle-based silhouette, clothing, proportions, and recognizable visual characteristics. The exaggerated hair must remain one of the dominant visual features.

Dumb Donald — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Dumb Donald, faithfully reproducing his distinctive hooded appearance, characteristic clothing, proportions, and recognizable visual design. The iconic hood must be physically real and naturally worn rather than appearing as a cartoon overlay.

Rudy — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Rudy, faithfully reproducing his distinctive hairstyle, clothing, proportions, facial characteristics, and recognizable swagger while rendering everything as believable real-world human appearance.

Weird Harold — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Weird Harold, faithfully reproducing his extremely distinctive tall, lanky appearance, long hair, clothing, proportions, and characteristic visual silhouette while making him look like a real human being.

Mushmouth — Transform the subject into a real-life version of Mushmouth, faithfully reproducing his distinctive facial characteristics, hairstyle, clothing, proportions, and recognizable visual design while rendering the character as a believable real person.

additionalInstructions:
CORE TRANSFORMATION:

• Completely transform the subject into the selected Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids character.
• The result must look like a REAL HUMAN interpretation of the character.
• Do not create a cartoon version of the subject.
• Do not simply apply photorealistic textures to a cartoon image.
• Do not place the cartoon character next to the subject.
• The subject themselves becomes the selected character.
• Preserve the selected character's defining silhouette, hairstyle, clothing, proportions, accessories, and visual traits.
• Translate those traits into believable real-world human anatomy, materials, fabric, hair, skin, and lighting.

IDENTITY AND RACE:

• Preserve the subject's race and skin tone rather than changing them to match an animated character's depicted race.
• The selected character's distinctive visual design should be reproduced through hairstyle, clothing, body shape, facial construction, accessories, and other appropriate traits.
• Do not use race as the primary mechanism for making the subject resemble the character.
• Preserve recognizable characteristics of the source subject where they can coexist with the selected character transformation.

CHARACTER-SPECIFIC FIDELITY:

• Fat Albert must have the unmistakably large, rounded body shape, characteristic hairstyle and iconic clothing associated with the character.
• Bucky must have his exceptionally large and distinctive hair as a dominant visual feature.
• Dumb Donald must have his instantly recognizable hood and characteristic outfit.
• Rudy must retain his recognizable hairstyle, clothing, proportions, and distinctive visual attitude.
• Weird Harold must retain his unusually tall, lanky proportions, distinctive hair, clothing, and silhouette.
• Mushmouth must retain his distinctive facial appearance, hairstyle, clothing, and proportions.
• Do not homogenize the characters into the same generic body type or costume.

REAL-LIFE TRANSLATION:

• Real human skin texture.
• Real individual hairs and physically plausible hairstyles.
• Real fabric and clothing construction.
• Realistic body anatomy adapted to the exaggerated character proportions.
• Physically believable lighting and shadows.
• Real photographic depth of field.
• The selected character must look as though they could actually exist in the photographed environment.
• Do not make the result look like CGI, animation, cosplay, a costume mascot, or a person wearing a cheap cartoon costume.
• The character traits must be inherent to the transformed subject.

HUMOR:

• The humor comes from the faithful real-life realization of the familiar cartoon design.
• Keep the transformation visually committed and deadpan rather than turning it into a caricature of the concept.
• Do not add joke text, captions, speech bubbles, or unrelated comedy props unless present in the source or specified by the master prompt.

ENVIRONMENT:

• Preserve the original environment unless the master prompt specifies otherwise.
• The selected character must physically occupy the existing environment.
• Lighting, perspective, scale, shadows, and reflections must integrate naturally.
• Do not add an artificial cartoon background.

MASTER PROMPT RULE:

• Master prompt instructions always override conflicting instructions EXCEPT the mandatory real-life transformation into the selected Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids character.
• Incorporate master-prompt clothing, pose, setting, action, camera angle, composition, and other information while maintaining the selected character's defining appearance.

FINAL VALIDATION:

✓ Exactly one selected character has been applied.
✓ The subject has become that character rather than standing beside the character.
✓ The character looks like a real human being.
✓ The character's defining physical traits are unmistakable.
✓ Fat Albert's distinctive girth is preserved when selected.
✓ Bucky's distinctive enormous hair is preserved when selected.
✓ Dumb Donald's iconic hood is preserved when selected.
✓ Rudy's distinctive appearance is preserved when selected.
✓ Weird Harold's tall, lanky appearance is preserved when selected.
✓ Mushmouth's distinctive appearance is preserved when selected.
✓ The subject's race and skin tone have not been changed merely to imitate the cartoon character.
✓ The result is photorealistic.
✓ The result does not look like a cartoon, CGI character, mascot, or costume.
✓ No unrelated characters or imagery have been added.
✓ If ANY answer is NO, regenerate until satisfied.

name: A BUG'S LIFE
message: Take a picture and completely reconstruct the image from the perspective of an ant standing at ground level. The camera must be extremely low to the ground, looking upward at the existing subject and environment so that ordinary human-scale objects become enormous towering structures. Preserve the existing visual content of the source image, but reinterpret its scale and perspective as though the viewer were a tiny ant moving through the scene.

options.text: Ground-Level Giant — extreme ant-eye perspective from directly beside the ground, making the existing subject and nearby objects tower dramatically overhead
Underfoot — camera positioned almost directly beneath the existing subject, looking upward at gigantic legs, shoes, furniture, or other visible structures
Ant's Journey — extremely low perspective moving through the existing environment, with ordinary objects becoming enormous obstacles and structures around the tiny viewpoint

additionalInstructions:
SCALE AND PERSPECTIVE:

• The defining transformation is EXTREME SCALE.
• The camera viewpoint must be approximately ant height above the ground.
• The viewer should feel only a few millimeters tall.
• Existing people, furniture, vehicles, buildings, plants, objects, and structures should appear enormous relative to the viewpoint.
• Look upward dramatically at nearby objects whenever the source composition permits.
• Use strong low-angle perspective and believable perspective convergence.
• Ground surfaces should occupy a substantial portion of the immediate foreground when appropriate.
• Nearby objects should loom dramatically overhead.
• Distant objects may recede toward the horizon and appear comparatively smaller.

SOURCE-CONTENT RESTRICTION:

• Use the existing visual content of the source image as the basis for the transformation.
• Do not invent unrelated giant objects merely to communicate scale.
• Do not replace the original environment with a generic insect world.
• Do not add random insects, flowers, mushrooms, leaves, or other miniature-world clichés unless they already exist in the source image or are explicitly required by the master prompt.
• The transformation comes from CAMERA HEIGHT, SCALE, PERSPECTIVE, and SPATIAL RECONSTRUCTION.

SUBJECT:

• Preserve the recognizable identity of the subject when a person is present.
• The subject should remain the same subject, merely perceived from an extremely tiny viewpoint.
• Do not turn the subject into an ant.
• Do not give the subject insect anatomy.
• If the subject is standing, the legs, shoes, lower body, and surrounding objects should feel gigantic from the ant's perspective.
• If the subject is seated, nearby furniture and body parts should similarly become towering structures.

PHOTOGRAPHIC REALISM:

• Photorealistic macro-scale perspective.
• Realistic depth of field appropriate to an extremely low camera position.
• Realistic ground-level texture.
• Physically believable lighting, shadows, reflections, and occlusion.
• Preserve realistic materials and surface textures.
• Avoid cartoon rendering despite the humorous scale concept.
• The result should look like a real photograph taken by an impossibly tiny camera.

MASTER PROMPT RULE:

• Master prompt instructions always override conflicting instructions EXCEPT the mandatory ant-scale, ground-level perspective transformation.
• Incorporate master-prompt clothing, pose, environment, action, objects, and composition while reconstructing the scene from the ant's viewpoint.

FINAL VALIDATION:

✓ Camera viewpoint is extremely close to ground level.
✓ The image clearly feels as though viewed by a tiny ant.
✓ Existing human-scale objects appear gigantic.
✓ The subject remains recognizable.
✓ The environment remains recognizable.
✓ Perspective and scale are physically convincing.
✓ No unnecessary invented miniature-world imagery has been added.
✓ The subject has not been turned into an insect.
✓ The result is photorealistic.
✓ If ANY answer is NO, regenerate until satisfied.

name: ZONE PLATE
message: Take a picture and reshoot it through a zone plate rather than a lens. Focus by diffraction gives a glowing, veiled image: highlights bleed into the shadows, edges never fully resolve, the whole frame carries a soft luminous haze, and contrast stays low with a dreamlike lift in the blacks.
additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Glowing halation spreading from highlights
• Edges that never fully resolve
• Low contrast with lifted blacks
• Even, luminous veil across the frame
• Subject recognisable through the glow
